issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect Milkable.messageOnMilk() to be a no-argument method returning a String (used in Main and described in the spec), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) with a double parameter and implements it in Goat and Seal. This parameter mismatch between solution and the specification/template will confuse students and prevents direct comparison with the provided Main/template usage which calls messageOnMilk() without arguments.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface and all implementations match the specification/template: change Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) to messageOnMilk() returning String, and update Goat and Seal implementations to implement messageOnMilk() without parameters (returning the string format described in the problem). Alternatively, if the intent is to include a volume parameter, update the problem statement, UML, and template Main calls to require and pass the double parameter consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a parameterless messageOnMilk() method (Milkable.messageOnMilk(): String) but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(double volume) and implements it with a double parameter in Goat and Seal. This changes the method signature for the same conceptual operation (milking an animal) and creates a mapping confusion for students: they will look for a parameterless method as described in the exercise and used in the template's Main, but the solution uses a different identifier/signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Milkable interface and its implementations use the parameterless signature messageOnMilk(): String to match the problem statement and template. Update Milkable.java to declare String messageOnMilk(); and change Goat and Seal implementations to return "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" without requiring a volume parameter. Adjust any calls accordingly.
